evidence.quoted_text:
def test_post_boundary_activation_refusal_is_required(self):
        phases = self._phases()
        manager = {"before": self._snapshot(10, "i1", "boot-1"),
                   "after": self._snapshot(11, "i2", "boot-1"),
                   "after_phase": {"direct": {"rc": 0},
                                   "dependency": {"rc": 1}}}
        reboot = {"before": self._snapshot(11, "i2", "boot-1"),
                  "after": self._snapshot(12, "i3", "boot-2"),
                  "after_phase": {"direct": {"rc": 1},
                                  "dependency": {"rc": 0}},
                  "boot_id_before": "boot-1", "boot_id_after": "boot-2",
                  "qemu_pid_before": 99, "qemu_pid_after": 99,
                  "qemu_identity_verified": True}
        checks = vm.build_checks(phases, manager, reboot)
        self.assertFalse(checks["mask_persisted"])
evidence.reason: The test only asserts the aggregate `mask_persisted` result while its fixtures deliberately leave one activation path succeeding after manager restart (`direct.rc == 0`) and one succeeding after reboot (`dependency.rc == 0`). A `build_checks` implementation that ignored either boundary would still make `mask_persisted` false, so the test does not independently prove both post-boundary refusal requirements. This is a concrete test-coverage defect in existing behavior, and the suggested fix is a routine test tightening rather than a new requirement.
